title: Mars medical autonomy, capability gaps and staffing-scale audit for OTA-TEC-0088
question: Source-grounded audit of the exact OTA-TEC-0088 Mars Medical Center dossier. Assess: (1) NASA/space-agency Earth-Independent Medical Operations requirements for long-duration exploration where rapid evacuation and real-time specialist support are unavailable; (2) which diagnostic, trauma, surgical, dental, laboratory, pharmacy and isolation capabilities are supported by current exploration-medicine evidence versus still-developmental concepts; (3) what Antarctica/McMurdo and other remote-medicine analogues can and cannot support when reasoning about a roughly 500-person Mars settlement; (4) whether any defensible staffing, cross-training, bed/cot, mass-casualty or medical-logistics scaling ranges can be derived without linear extrapolation from terrestrial hospitals; (5) medicine shelf life, blood availability, walking-blood-bank concepts, sterilization and critical consumables under multi-year resupply constraints; and (6) wording that should remain [H]/[OFFEN] rather than [R]. Do NOT create fictional population, staffing, bed-count, cost, treatment-rate, event-frequency or NOXIA balancing values.
why_now: OTA-TEC-0088 is a mapped OTA->NOXIA object still reported uncovered and explicitly remains ENTWURF pending source-pinned staffing/capability/Walking-Blood-Bank review. Medical autonomy is a distinct safety-critical evidence domain and should not be inferred from generic colony analogies.
real_world_anchor: NASA Earth-Independent Medical Operations and exploration medical capability research; Antarctic/remote medicine analogues; blood, pharmaceutical, sterilization and telemedicine constraints in isolated operations.
novelty_reason: First exact-source medical-autonomy audit for the mapped Mars Medical Center; existing OTA tech audits do not cover colony-scale healthcare capability and logistics.
